chunks: Or like the one who passed by a town which was ruined upon its rooftops. He said: 'How can God give life to this after its death?' So God made him die for a hundred years, then raised him. He said: 'How long did you stay?' He said: 'I stayed a day or part of a day.' He said: 'No, you stayed a hundred years. So look at your food and your drink; it has not decomposed. And look at your donkey! And We shall make you a sign for the people. And look at the bones, how We raise them, then We clothe them with flesh.' When it became clear to him, he said: 'I know that God is Powerful over all things.'
ai.seo_question: What is the story of the man who died for a hundred years and was resurrected in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this verse is often attributed to Uzair (Ezra), whose prolonged sleep served as a tangible miracle to affirm the reality of bodily resurrection for the people of his time. The narrative emphasizes not only the physical reassembly of bones but also the preservation of sustenance, illustrating God's absolute power over time and matter as a sign (ayah) for humanity.
